Ten Predictions for AI in 2027

Where the frontier labs are heading, as ten dated predictions with a confidence, the evidence, and what would prove each wrong. The AI Market Map will mark each one right or wrong on its check date.

FrontierAGI Research
November 18, 2026 · 7 min read · ⚠️ = secondary source
Key takeawaysThe predictionsWhere the labs are less likely to goMethod and sources

⚡ Key takeaways

💡
  1. Most confident (85%): every frontier lab sells its own agent platform by mid-2027.
  2. Restricted tiers for cyber and bio become standard (75%); more labs publish self-improvement ratings (70%).
  3. Prices halve again (70%) while open models stay within six months of the frontier (60%).
  4. Most enterprise agent pilots still stall (65%).
  5. Labs are less likely to certify each other or run inside customers' data centres (55%).

🔧 Reproduce this: predictions.py
predictions.py · reads data/predictions-2027.json
"""predictions.py — the Interlude's ten predictions for 2027, ready to be scored later.

Reads data/predictions-2027.json. Prints each claim with its confidence and check date,
the expected number that come true if the confidences are honest, and how they will be
scored (Brier score = mean of (confidence - outcome)^2 once outcomes are known).
Standard library only.
"""
import json, os
d = json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "..", "..", "predictions-2027.json")))
for p in sorted(d["items"], key=lambda p: (p["check"], -p["conf"])):
    print(f"#{p['id']:2d} {p['conf']:.0%} by {p['check']}  {p['claim'][:78]}")
exp = sum(p["conf"] for p in d["items"])
print(f"expected to come true if calibrated: {exp:.1f} of {len(d['items'])}")
done = [p for p in d["items"] if p["outcome"] is not None]
print(f"scored so far: {len(done)}" + (f", Brier {sum((p['conf'] - p['outcome']) ** 2 for p in done) / len(done):.3f}" if done else " (first checks due 2027-06)"))

So what: A forecast you cannot be wrong about is not a forecast; these will be scored in public.

📊 Where the labs are less likely to go

  • Our reading.
    • Inside customers' own data centres.
    • Certifying other labs' models.
    • Customer-specific test environments built over years.
    • Sovereign deployments that require local control.

📄 Method and sources

  • Confidences are our judgement; evidence comes from the site's sourced maps and the surveys in Brief 4.
  • Scoring: Brier score, the mean of (confidence − outcome)² once outcomes are known.
  • Outcomes are recorded in data/predictions-2027.json and shown on the AI Market Map.

Facts are sourced; figures marked ⚠️ come from secondary reports or company statements. Scores, weights and predictions are our judgement and are labelled.
